banh-te-phu-nhi.name: Phu Nhi rice cakes
banh-te-phu-nhi.serving_basis: About eight slender cakes, two per person, served warm with a light dipping sauce.
banh-te-phu-nhi.description: Phu Nhi rice cakes are a Xu Doai specialty made from wet-ground rice batter and filled with pork, wood-ear mushrooms and shallots before being wrapped in leaves and boiled. Bếp Việt adapts the traditional technique for a small home batch, stirring the batter until smooth and pliable without letting it become pasty.
banh-te-phu-nhi.finished_dish: Each warm cake has a neat slender shape, a tender ivory rice casing and a savory pork filling with lightly crisp mushrooms and fragrant shallots.
banh-te-phu-nhi.serving: Unwrap while warm and enjoy with pickled vegetables or a little dipping sauce. Re-steam briefly if the cakes cool; avoid boiling them again, which can make the casing waterlogged.
tips: Soak the rice until soft, then blend it thoroughly; strain if any coarse grains remain.
Stir the batter over low heat until just thickened and still pliable. Overcooked batter is difficult to spread around the filling.
Wrap the leaves snugly but leave room for expansion, then tie gently so the cakes cook evenly without splitting.
search_terms: Vietnamese pork rice cakes in leaves
banh-te-phu-nhi.image_alt: Phu Nhi rice cakes wrapped in green leaves, with one opened to show a tender rice casing and pork and wood-ear mushroom filling; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-te-phu-nhi.time_note: About 4 hours 35 minutes, including three hours to soak the rice; the rice can be soaked overnight.

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse, soak for three hours, then drain.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Blend with the rice; add gradually so the batter does not become too thin.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: Finely minced; a little fat keeps the filling moist.

ingredients.name: Dried wood-ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Rehydrate, rinse well and mince.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Finely minced.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the filling; adjust for saltiness.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Freshly ground if available.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For the filling and to prevent batter from sticking.

ingredients.name: Banana or dong leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash, briefly blanch to soften, then wipe dry.

preparation_steps: Rinse the rice, soak in clean water for three hours and drain. Blend with about 500 ml water until smooth, working in batches if needed.
Rehydrate the wood-ear mushrooms, rinse and mince. Mince the pork and shallots, then season with fish sauce and pepper.
Sauté the shallots in oil, add the pork and cook until crumbly. Add the mushrooms, stir until the filling is fairly dry, then season to taste.
Wash and briefly blanch the leaves to make them pliable. Wipe them dry and prepare ties and a pot of water.
cooking_steps: Pour the rice batter into a heavy saucepan. Stir constantly over low heat; when it begins to thicken, remove from the heat and keep stirring until smooth and pliable but still spreadable.
Spread a thin layer of batter lengthwise on a leaf, add a line of filling and cover with a little more batter. Fold into a slender parcel, tuck in both ends and tie gently.
Place the parcels in gently boiling water and cook for 35–40 minutes, depending on their size. Turn them once; the casing should look slightly translucent with no raw batter at the center.
Lift out, drain and rest for five minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers and re-steam the same day before eating.

banh-ram-it-hue.name: Hue bánh ram ít
aliases: Shrimp and pork bánh ram ít
banh-ram-it-hue.serving_basis: About twelve small dumplings, three per person, served while the crispy bases are fresh.
banh-ram-it-hue.description: Hue bánh ram ít combines two textures in one bite: a soft glutinous-rice dumpling filled with shrimp and pork, set on a crisp fried rice base. Bếp Việt edits a home-sized batch with lightly seasoned filling and a sweet-sour fish sauce for serving.
banh-ram-it-hue.finished_dish: A golden crisp base supports a tender ivory dumpling with savory shrimp and pork, a little scallion oil and a gentle chili-lime dip.
banh-ram-it-hue.serving: Assemble each dumpling on its crispy base just before serving. Eat warm with lightly sweetened garlic-chili fish sauce to balance the richness and chewiness.
tips: Add warm water to the glutinous-rice flour gradually until the dough is smooth and not sticky.
Steam the bases first, let them cool and pat dry before frying to make them crisp with less splatter.
Cook the filling until fairly dry and let it cool before wrapping so the dough does not become soggy.
banh-ram-it-hue.image_alt: Hue bánh ram ít on a plate, each shrimp and pork sticky-rice dumpling resting on a crisp golden base; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-ram-it-hue.time_note: About 1 hour 35 minutes, including a 15-minute dough rest; fry the bases in small batches to keep them crisp.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift before use.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually until the dough is pliable; actual absorption varies.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel, devein and mince.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Finely minced.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Finely minced.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Slice finely for scallion oil.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the filling and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Divide between the filling and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Finely minced.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Juice for the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the bases; a small pan reduces the amount needed.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the dough.

ingredients.name: Ground pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the filling.

preparation_steps: Mix the glutinous-rice flour with salt. Gradually add warm water and knead until smooth and non-sticky. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Mince the shrimp and pork belly. Season with some fish sauce, sugar, pepper and shallots; leave for ten minutes.
Mix the remaining fish sauce and sugar with warm water, lime juice, garlic and chili. Stir to dissolve and taste.
cooking_steps: Divide the dough into twelve portions. Shape half into flat bases and the rest into small filled dumplings; place on lightly oiled banana leaves.
Steam for 12–15 minutes, until the dough turns translucent and the filling is fully cooked. Cool slightly and pat the bases dry.
Fry the bases over medium heat until golden and crisp, then drain. Brush the soft dumplings with a little scallion oil if desired.
Set one dumpling on each crisp base, garnish with scallion and serve at once with the dipping sauce. Do not stack while hot.

canh-kiem-nam-bo.name: Southern Vietnamese canh kiểm
canh-kiem-nam-bo.serving_basis: One pot of about 1.5 litres, served with steamed rice or fresh rice vermicelli.
canh-kiem-nam-bo.description: Canh kiểm is a Southern Vietnamese vegetarian soup that simmers a variety of vegetables in coconut liquid and is often served at vegetarian meals and offerings. Bếp Việt edits a home version with pumpkin, sweet potato, taro, green banana, long beans, mushrooms, tofu skin and peanuts; the ingredients are added in stages so tender vegetables keep their shape.
canh-kiem-nam-bo.finished_dish: A pale-golden coconut broth carries the natural sweetness of pumpkin and root vegetables. Each piece of vegetable, mushroom and tofu skin stays distinct, creating a gently rich plant-based soup.
canh-kiem-nam-bo.serving: Serve hot with rice or vermicelli. Ladle gently so the vegetables stay intact; if using thick coconut cream, dilute it to keep the broth from becoming heavy.
tips: Briefly pan-sear the taro to help it hold its shape and develop a nutty flavor.
Add pumpkin and long beans after the slower-cooking roots so they do not overcook.
Use coconut milk in moderation and season at the end, since the vegetables vary in natural sweetness.
search_terms: Vietnamese vegetarian pumpkin and taro soup
canh-kiem-nam-bo.image_alt: A bowl of Southern Vietnamese canh kiểm with pale coconut broth, pumpkin, roots, green banana, long beans, mushrooms, peanuts and tofu skin; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove seeds and cut into even pieces.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into cubes.

ingredients.name: Taro
ingredients.notes: Peel and cube; optionally pan-sear.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Peel, soak briefly in salted water and slice.

ingredients.name: Long beans
ingredients.notes: Trim and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Fresh shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Wipe clean and halve if large.

ingredients.name: Tofu skin
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, cut into pieces and check the label for animal-derived seasonings.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Roast and remove the skins.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Use plain coconut milk; dilute if it is very thick.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust to cover the vegetables.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Reduce if the vegetables are naturally sweet.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For pan-searing the taro if desired.

preparation_steps: Peel and cube the pumpkin, sweet potato and taro. Soak the sliced green banana in lightly salted water to slow browning, then rinse.
Trim the long beans and clean the mushrooms. Soak the tofu skin in warm water until soft, gently squeeze and cut.
If desired, lightly pan-sear the taro in a little oil until the outside is just set.
cooking_steps: Bring the water and half the coconut milk to a simmer. Add sweet potato, taro and green banana; cook over medium heat for 12–15 minutes until nearly tender.
Add pumpkin, long beans, mushrooms and tofu skin. Simmer for 8–10 minutes, keeping the broth gentle so the vegetables do not break apart.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, season with salt and a little sugar, then simmer for 3–4 minutes. Taste and turn off the heat once the pumpkin is just tender.
Scatter roasted peanuts over the soup. Serve hot with rice or vermicelli; refrigerate leftovers and bring them to a full boil before serving again.

bun-chay-hue.name: Hue vegetarian bún soup
aliases: Mushroom and tofu bún in Hue style
bun-chay-hue.serving_basis: Four generous bowls with mushrooms, tofu, bamboo shoots and wheat gluten.
bun-chay-hue.description: Hue vegetarian bún is a fragrant noodle soup built around mushrooms and lemongrass, served with rice vermicelli, fried tofu, wheat gluten, bamboo shoots and greens. Bếp Việt edits a fully plant-based home version with a vegetable-and-mushroom broth; check packaged seasonings to avoid animal-derived ingredients.
bun-chay-hue.finished_dish: A hot bowl with clear lemongrass-scented broth, gentle mushroom sweetness, golden tofu, tender chewy wheat gluten and green vegetables makes a light but satisfying meal.
bun-chay-hue.serving: Blanch the noodles separately, place them in bowls, then ladle over the simmering broth with mushrooms, bamboo shoots, tofu and wheat gluten. Add herbs, pepper or chili and serve at once so the noodles stay springy.
tips: Boil dried bamboo shoots twice, changing the water, and taste them before cooking to reduce bitterness and strong aromas.
Sauté the mushrooms and wheat gluten before adding them to deepen the flavor of both the toppings and broth.
Use leek in place of onion and garlic if desired, and verify that packaged seasoning is fully plant-based.
bun-chay-hue.image_alt: A bowl of Hue vegetarian bún with white rice vermicelli, fried tofu, wheat gluten, mushrooms, bamboo shoots and herbs in lemongrass broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
bun-chay-hue.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 20 minutes to soak bamboo shoots and mushrooms; pre-cooked fresh bamboo shoots shorten the preparation.

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Briefly blanch and drain.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into pieces, pat dry, then fry or pan-sear until golden.

ingredients.name: Wheat gluten
ingredients.notes: Slice into bite-size pieces and choose a plant-based product.

ingredients.name: Dried bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Soak, boil twice in fresh water and shred.

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Rehydrate; strain the soaking liquid if using it in the broth.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Clean and halve.

ingredients.name: Napa cabbage
ingredients.notes: Cut into short pieces.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise and cut into lengths; reserve a little minced lemongrass.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Slice; use in place of onion for a plant-based version.

ingredients.name: Vegetable stock
ingredients.notes: Use a broth made from vegetables and mushrooms, not bones.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a plant-based product.

ingredients.name: Annatto oil
ingredients.notes: Optional, for a gentle golden-orange hue.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the broth.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust lightly for balance.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs and pepper
ingredients.notes: Wash, drain and use to taste.

preparation_steps: Soak the dried bamboo shoots and shiitake mushrooms in warm water for about 20 minutes. Boil the bamboo shoots twice in fresh water, then shred and rinse.
Cut the tofu and wheat gluten. Clean the straw mushrooms, napa cabbage, lemongrass and leek; set aside bruised lemongrass and a little minced portion.
Blanch the noodles briefly and divide among four bowls. Strain the mushroom soaking liquid through a fine sieve if using.
cooking_steps: Sauté the leek and minced lemongrass in oil. Add wheat gluten, both mushrooms and bamboo shoots; stir-fry for 3–4 minutes with a little soy sauce.
Bring the vegetable stock and bruised lemongrass to a boil. Add the sautéed toppings, tofu and strained mushroom liquid; lower the heat and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add napa cabbage and cook just until tender. Season with salt, a little sugar, soy sauce and optional annatto oil; taste for a fragrant, gently savory broth.
Remove the lemongrass stalks. Ladle the broth and toppings over the noodles, add herbs and pepper, and serve hot.

banh-gai-tu-tru.name: Tu Tru ramie-leaf cakes
banh-gai-tu-tru.serving_basis: About eight small cakes, two per person, served cooled with hot tea.
banh-gai-tu-tru.description: Tu Tru bánh gai from Mia village in Tho Xuan is known for a dark glutinous-rice casing made with ramie leaves, a mung-bean and coconut filling, gentle molasses sweetness and sesame. Bếp Việt adapts a small batch with softened dried ramie leaves and ordinary home equipment; the parcels are wrapped in banana leaf, steamed and cooled so the casing becomes pleasantly chewy.
banh-gai-tu-tru.finished_dish: Each small square cake has a glossy dark casing with the fragrance of ramie leaves, a sweet mung-bean and coconut center, a hint of molasses and a lightly nutty sesame finish.
banh-gai-tu-tru.serving: Let the cakes cool completely before peeling the inner leaf, since the casing is sticky. Serve in small pieces with hot tea; briefly steam again if a refrigerated cake becomes firm.
tips: Cook the ramie leaves until very soft, then blend or pound finely; fibrous leaves make the casing rough.
Cook the filling until it just holds together when rolled; drying it too much makes the center crumbly.
Wrap the parcels securely and steam over steady medium heat. Let them dry and cool before stacking so condensation does not collect on the leaves.
search_terms: Vietnamese mung bean coconut ramie cake
banh-gai-tu-tru.image_alt: Tu Tru bánh gai with a dark ramie-leaf casing, sesame and a mung-bean coconut center, wrapped in banana leaf; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-gai-tu-tru.time_note: About 4 hours 25 minutes, including three hours to soak the mung beans and ramie leaves; these can be soaked ahead.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift before use.

ingredients.name: Dried ramie leaves
ingredients.notes: Soak, rinse and simmer until tender; remove tough ribs.

ingredients.name: Sugarcane molasses
ingredients.notes: Adds gentle sweetness and color; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak for three hours, then steam until tender.

ingredients.name: Grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Use mature coconut, finely grated.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Cook with the mung beans; reduce if the molasses is very sweet.

ingredients.name: White sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Toast and use lightly on the outside of the cakes.

ingredients.name: Banana essence
ingredients.notes: Optional; use only a few drops.

ingredients.name: Dried banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Wipe clean and warm briefly to soften; line with fresh leaves if brittle.

preparation_steps: Soak the mung beans for about three hours, rinse and steam until tender. Soak, rinse and boil the dried ramie leaves until soft; squeeze dry and blend with a little of the cooking water.
Mash the warm mung beans. Cook with sugar over low heat, add the grated coconut and stir until the filling comes together. Cool and divide into eight balls.
Mix the glutinous-rice flour with the ramie puree and molasses. Knead until the dough is evenly dark, pliable and smooth; add only a few drops of banana essence if using.
Warm the banana leaves until pliable, wipe clean and cut into wrappers. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
cooking_steps: Divide the dough into eight portions. Flatten each portion, add a filling ball, seal completely and shape into a small flat square; lightly roll in toasted sesame.
Place each cake on banana leaf and wrap securely. Arrange with space between cakes in a steamer and bring the water to a boil first.
Steam over medium heat for about 25–30 minutes. Keep the water steadily simmering and avoid opening the lid repeatedly; the cooked casing should look glossy and smell of ramie leaves.
Remove the cakes and let them cool and dry completely before serving. Keep covered for the day; briefly steam again if the casing firms up.
